details:
Space Twins is an interactive 3D planetary analog explorer designed to demonstrate geological similarities between Earth, Mars, and the Moon.

The project features 17 geological locations: 8 on Earth, 5 on Mars, and 4 on the Moon. It allows users to explore three interactive 3D planetary models, rotate the worlds, select highlighted locations, and discover geological similarities through detailed information cards.

Users can compare locations based on shared geological features, including impact craters, volcanic formations, basaltic rocks, dry landscapes, sedimentary layers, and polar conditions. Each location includes scientific descriptions, suggested geological analogs, and links to NASA's image archive for further exploration.

The project also includes an interactive 3D exploration mode where users can land on selected planetary environments, navigate procedurally generated terrain, jump, and collect scientific samples while learning about planetary conditions such as gravity.

Space Twins addresses the challenge of making planetary geology accessible and engaging. By connecting familiar environments on Earth with landscapes on other worlds, it demonstrates how Earth can serve as a natural laboratory for understanding planetary surfaces and preparing for future exploration.

The project was developed using HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, Three.js, WebGL, SVG, and the HTML Canvas API.

Its creative approach combines scientific research, interactive 3D visualization, geological comparisons, and exploration gameplay in one educational experience.

During development, the team considered scientific accuracy, the relevance of geological similarities, user experience, accessibility, and the limitations of browser-based 3D rendering.
